 SCOTUS Gives Trump a Win on Border Wall 
 Ruling lifts injunction on contested 341-mile Big Bend construction 
 By 
 Rob Quinn 
 with Newser.AI 
 Posted Nov 9, 2026 3:16 PM CST 
 Copied 
 A portion of border wall is under construction in the Big Bend region, Sept. 23, 2026, near Sierra Blanca, Texas.   (AP Photo/John Locher, File) 
 See 2 more photos 
 The Supreme Court just cleared the way for new border wall construction in one of the most remote stretches of the US-Mexico line. In a brief, unsigned ruling Monday, the justices lifted a lower-court order that had paused work in Texas' Big Bend region while a lawsuit played out, saying the judge who issued it lacked authority and that President Trump's administration is "extremely likely to prevail," NBC News reports. Last month, a federal judge issued a preliminary injunction halting "ground-disturbing activities" linked to border wall projects in the region. 
 The 341-mile project, which runs through Big Bend National Park and along the Rio Grande, has drawn fire from environmental advocates and local groups who warn of harm to wildlife and historic sites, including a 100-year-old church. The court cited "compelling interests" in border security; only Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson dissented. The plan to build 30-foot steel walls in the area drew bipartisan opposition in the region, with critics calling it a waste of money in an area that sees relatively few border crossings, the AP reports. They argued that drones and other surveillance technology would be enough protect the border in the area. The administration said roughly 89,000 people have been detained crossing in the area in recent years, and argued that the region would see more illegal traffic if there was a gap in the border wall.
